newsitem.title: USA: Calif. earthquake agency responds to Barstow quake.
newsitem.headline: Calif. earthquake agency responds to Barstow quake.

text.p: The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) said it dispatched its disaster response coordinator to survey potential damage from a moderate earthquake that shook southern California on Tuesday.
The CEA said the earthquake was the first to affect residential property in the state since the authority began selling insurance policies in December.
Tuesday's quake measured 5.4 on the open-ended Richter scale and was an aftershock to the Landers earthquake that struck in June 1992 with a 7.3 magnitude.
Its epicentre was 12 miles northeast of Barstow in the Mojave Desert, 100 miles northeast of Los Angeles.
The CEA said it has about 100 policyholders in a 20-mile area surrounding the earthquake epicenter. By late Tuesday, the CEA said it knew of no policyholders who had filed claims.
The CEA is a public-private authority created to offer basic earthquake insurance coverage in California.
